title: Hereditary cotorsion pairs lifted to cochain complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Let $(\mathcal F,\mathcal T)$ be a hereditary cotorsion pair: $\mathcal F={}^{\perp_1}\mathcal T$, $\mathcal T=\mathcal F^{\perp_1}$, and $\operatorname{Ext}^i(F,T)=0$ for every $i\geq1$, $F\in\mathcal F$ and $T\in\mathcal T$. Ext means Yoneda extensions, so vanishing of Ext in degree one means all short exact extensions split. Assume that $\mathcal F$ contains a generator $G$ and that $\mathcal T=S^{\perp_1}$ for a set $S\subseteq\mathcal F$. A generator means every object is an epimorphic image of a small coproduct of its copies.
Work in $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A)$, the category of integer-indexed cochain complexes with differentials $d^{n+1}d^n=0$. Write $\mathcal W$ for complexes with zero cohomology. Let $\widetilde{\mathcal F}$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal T}$ be the acyclic complexes whose cycles lie in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal T$, respectively. For complexes $P,T$, use the complex of abelian groups $\operatorname{Hom}^r(P,T)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(P^n,T^{n+r})$ with differential $\delta h=d_T h-(-1)^r h d_P$. Define $\operatorname{dg}\mathcal F$ to consist of complexes with terms in $\mathcal F$ whose Hom complex into every object of $\widetilde{\mathcal T}$ is acyclic. Define $\operatorname{dg}\mathcal T$ to consist of complexes with terms in $\mathcal T$ whose Hom complex from every object of $\widetilde{\mathcal F}$ is acyclic.
Then $(\operatorname{dg}\mathcal F,\widetilde{\mathcal T})$ and $(\widetilde{\mathcal F},\operatorname{dg}\mathcal T)$ are hereditary cotorsion pairs in $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal A)$, and
$$\operatorname{dg}\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W=\widetilde{\mathcal F},\qquad \operatorname{dg}\mathcal T\cap\mathcal W=\widetilde{\mathcal T}.$$
Here hereditary for the induced pairs includes closure of the left class under kernels of epimorphisms between its objects and closure of the right class under cokernels of monomorphisms between its objects. If $S^nA$ denotes the complex with $A$ in degree $n$ and zero in the other degrees, then
$$\widetilde{\mathcal T}=\{S^nA:n\in\mathbf Z,\ A\in S\cup\{G\}\}^{\perp_1}.$$
These assertions do not assume enough projectives in $\mathcal A$, and do not assert set cogeneration of the second induced pair.
